seo_title: Solar Marketing Agency in Faridabad: Homes vs Factories
description: Solar marketing agency in Faridabad guide: how to run separate residential and commercial solar campaigns for Faridabad homes, societies and industrial units.
headline: Solar marketing agency in Faridabad: running separate campaigns for homes and factories
card_text: Faridabad installers sell to sector houses, Greater Faridabad societies and Mathura Road factories. Here's why each needs its own campaign, message and follow-up.
intro:
A solar marketing agency in Faridabad has to market two different products to two different buyers. One is a 3–10 kW rooftop system for a family in Sector 15, 16 or 21, a builder floor in NIT or a flat owner in a Greater Faridabad society. The other is a 50 kW to several hundred kW plant for a factory owner along Mathura Road or in the Faridabad–Ballabgarh industrial belt, who thinks in payback months and power bills, not subsidies.

Most installers in the city run one campaign for both, and it shows: homeowners get calls about load studies, and factory owners see ads about the PM Surya Ghar subsidy they can't claim. This guide explains how to split your marketing into a residential track and a commercial track, what each needs to say, which channels suit each, and how to measure both without mixing them up.

sections.h2: Why Faridabad needs two solar campaigns, not one
sections.html:
Faridabad is one of Haryana's oldest industrial towns, and it is also a large residential city. That mix is the opportunity and the trap. The two buyers differ on almost every point that matters to your marketing:

Residential buyerCommercial or industrial buyer
Who decidesHomeowner and family; RWA for common areasOwner, director or plant head; often a finance person too
Typical system3–10 kW on a house or builder floorTens to hundreds of kW on a shed or warehouse roof
Main reason to buyLower monthly bill, subsidy, rising tariffsCost per unit, payback period, cash flow
SubsidyPM Surya Ghar central assistance for eligible homesNot eligible for the residential subsidy
Sales cycleDays to a few weeksWeeks to months, with proposals and site audits
Best first stepFree rooftop surveyBill analysis and feasibility visit

When these two share one ad account, one landing page and one sales script, the cheaper residential leads drown out the commercial ones, and your team never learns which ads actually bring factory enquiries. Separate campaigns, forms, landing pages and lead sheets fix that.

sections.h2: Faridabad facts both campaigns must get right
sections.html:
Buyers in Faridabad compare several quotes, and a wrong fact on a call loses trust quickly. Check these before you write ads or scripts:

  • DISCOM: Faridabad is served by Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN). Net-metering applications, feasibility checks and the bi-directional meter go through DHBVN, and larger systems also need electrical safety approval from the state's Chief Electrical Inspector. Tell buyers who files what, and how long it usually takes.
  • Sanctioned load and transformer capacity: a rooftop system generally can't exceed the connection's sanctioned load, and DHBVN also checks spare capacity on the local transformer. Some older sectors have crowded transformers, so set expectations on the first call instead of after the survey.
  • Central subsidy for homes: PM Surya Ghar offers central financial assistance to eligible households, currently capped at ₹78,000 for systems of 3 kW and above, with a per-kW rate for housing society common areas. Check pmsuryaghar.gov.in for current amounts before each campaign.
  • State support: Haryana is pushing rooftop solar hard under PM Surya Ghar and has announced extra help, such as interest-free assistance for some consumers and support for lower-income families. Sources disagree on the exact amounts, so quote a state figure only from the current order of the Haryana renewable energy department or DHBVN.
  • Housing societies: in societies with a single-point bulk connection, the RWA is DHBVN's consumer, so individual flat owners usually can't get their own net meter. Sell common-area solar to the RWA instead.

For safe subsidy wording in ads, see our guide to PM Surya Ghar subsidy ads.

sections.h2: The residential track: sector houses, NIT and Greater Faridabad
sections.html:
Faridabad's homes fall into three groups, and each wants a slightly different message:

  1. Independent houses in the older sectors (such as 14, 15, 16, 21 and 37). Owners control the roof and usually pay large summer bills. Lead with bill savings and the subsidy, and show installations on similar houses.
  2. Builder floors and houses in NIT, Old Faridabad and Ballabgarh. Roof rights are often shared or unclear, so ask early who owns the roof and whether the other floors agree. Ads that show small, neat systems on shared roofs work better here than big villa photos.
  3. High-rise societies in Greater Faridabad. Flat owners rarely decide alone. Your target is the RWA committee and the facility manager, with a proposal for common-area solar on lifts, pumps and lighting.

For the first two groups, Meta lead ads targeted to Faridabad pincodes, Google Search ads on phrases like "solar panel installation in Faridabad" and a well-kept Google Business Profile do most of the work. Use a short form with qualifying questions: own house or rented, monthly bill range, roof type and pincode. Our Facebook ads for solar installers guide covers the full lead form setup.

sections.h2: The commercial track: Mathura Road and the industrial sectors
sections.html:
Faridabad's factories, from small fabrication units to large auto-component and engineering plants, are a strong solar market because their roofs are big and their power bills are a real cost line. But a factory owner doesn't respond to the same ad as a homeowner. The commercial track needs:

  • A different promise. Talk about cost per unit, payback period and protection from tariff increases. Offer a free bill analysis: "Send us your last three electricity bills and we'll estimate your savings and payback."
  • Different keywords. Bid on searches like "commercial solar Faridabad", "industrial solar EPC", "solar for factory" and "rooftop solar for warehouse". Exclude "subsidy", "free" and "home" in this campaign so residential searchers don't use the budget.
  • Different channels. Search ads and LinkedIn reach decision-makers better than broad Meta audiences. Direct outreach to units in known industrial sectors, industry association events and referrals from existing commercial clients often bring the best projects.
  • Different proof. Case studies with system size, roof type and the approval steps you handled carry more weight than reviews from homeowners. If you have commercial installations, photograph them and write them up.
  • A longer follow-up. Expect a site audit, a proposal, a revision and a finance discussion. Track every stage so you know which campaign brought projects that actually signed.

sections.h2: What a solar marketing agency in Faridabad should set up
sections.html:
Whether you hire an agency or do it in-house, the setup for a Faridabad installer should include:

  1. Two separate campaigns in Google Ads and Meta, one residential and one commercial, each with its own budget.
  2. Two landing pages: a residential page with a subsidy explainer, savings estimate and WhatsApp button, and a commercial page with a bill-analysis form and project examples.
  3. Location targeting by Faridabad pincodes and sectors your team can actually serve, with nearby areas such as Palwal added only if you install there.
  4. A Google Business Profile with photos from Faridabad jobs, correct service areas and a steady flow of reviews. Our guide on getting more Google reviews has a simple process.
  5. One lead sheet or CRM with a "track" column, so residential and commercial leads are never counted together.
  6. Call tracking and a rule for response time, ideally a call within minutes during working hours.

At Performance and Pixel we work with 30+ solar EPCs and manufacturers across India, and this split is one of the first changes we make for installers who sell to both homes and businesses. Our solar marketing agency page explains how we run these campaigns across Delhi NCR, and our solar portfolio shows the four solar case studies.

There is no fixed split that suits every installer. A useful starting point is to put most of the budget into the track that matches your team's strength, then move money based on site visits and signed orders, not lead counts. Residential leads are usually cheaper and faster; commercial leads are fewer and slower, but one project can be worth many home installations.

For reference, our rooftop solar campaigns have brought qualified residential enquiries at ₹60–80 each, and solar clients at scale typically get 20–30 leads a day and 5–10 site visits a week. Your numbers will depend on your offer, service area, follow-up speed and season, and nobody can honestly guarantee results. Commercial cost per lead will be higher, and that is normal.

Review both tracks every week: leads, connected calls, surveys or audits booked, proposals sent and orders won. Our post on performance marketing for solar companies explains why cost per site visit is the number to watch.

• Showing subsidy ads to factory owners. They aren't eligible for the residential subsidy, and it makes you look like a home-only installer.
  • Targeting "Faridabad + 40 km". That radius pulls in south Delhi, Noida and Gurugram, where you may not install. Target the sectors and pincodes you serve.
  • Ignoring roof rights. In builder floors and societies, a lead who doesn't control the roof rarely converts. Ask on the form.
  • Promising timelines you don't control. DHBVN approvals and meter installation take time. Give a typical range and keep customers updated.
  • No commercial proof. If your website only shows home rooftops, factory owners will assume you can't handle their project.

faqs: What does a solar marketing agency in Faridabad do?

It plans and runs the ads, website, Google Business Profile and lead follow-up that bring rooftop solar enquiries for installers in Faridabad. A good one runs residential and commercial campaigns separately and reports on site visits and signed orders, not just leads.
Which DISCOM handles net metering in Faridabad?

Faridabad is served by Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN). Net-metering applications, feasibility checks and the bi-directional meter are handled by DHBVN. Check DHBVN's current process and documents before you explain it to customers.
Can factories in Faridabad get the PM Surya Ghar subsidy?

No. PM Surya Ghar central assistance is for eligible residential households and housing society common areas, not commercial or industrial connections. Market commercial solar on savings and payback instead.
Is Google Ads or Meta better for solar leads in Faridabad?

For homes, both work well: Meta lead ads for volume and Google Search for buyers already looking. For factories and warehouses, Google Search, LinkedIn and direct outreach usually reach decision-makers better than broad Meta audiences.
